# pigz - Parallel Implementation of GZip

pigz (pronounced "pig-zee") is a parallel implementation of gzip that compresses files using multiple processors and cores.

## What pigz does

pigz is a fully functional replacement for gzip that exploits multiple processors and multiple cores to compress data faster. It can compress and decompress files in gzip, zlib, and zip formats.

## Basic Usage

```
pigz [options] [files...]
unpigz [options] [files...]
```

If no files are specified or "-" is given as a filename, pigz reads from standard input.

## Key Features

- **Parallel compression**: Splits input into chunks (default 128 KB) and compresses them in parallel
- **Multiple output formats**: Supports gzip, zlib, and single-entry zip formats
- **Compatible with gzip**: Can decompress any gzip file; gzip can decompress any pigz-compressed file
- **Independent blocks**: Optional mode for partial error recovery and random access
- **rsyncable**: Optional mode for rsync-friendly output

## Common Options

- **-#** (1-9, 11): Set compression level (1=fastest, 9=best, 11=zopfli for maximum compression)
- **-d, --decompress**: Decompress files
- **-k, --keep**: Keep original files (don't delete after compression)
- **-c, --stdout**: Write output to stdout
- **-p n**: Use n processors (default: all available)
- **-b n**: Set block size to n KB (default: 128)
- **-i, --independent**: Compress blocks independently
- **-R, --rsyncable**: Make output rsync-friendly
- **-l, --list**: List contents of compressed files
- **-t, --test**: Test integrity of compressed files
- **-f, --force**: Force overwrite of output files
- **-r, --recursive**: Recursively compress directories
- **-z, --zlib**: Use zlib format instead of gzip
- **-K, --zip**: Use zip format (single entry)
- **-v, --verbose**: Verbose output
- **-h, --help**: Display help

## Examples

Compress a file using all available processors:
```
pigz file.txt
```

Compress with maximum compression (slower):
```
pigz -11 file.txt
```

Decompress a file:
```
pigz -d file.txt.gz
# or
unpigz file.txt.gz
```

Compress to stdout:
```
pigz -c file.txt > file.txt.gz
```

Compress with 4 processors and keep the original:
```
pigz -k -p 4 file.txt
```

Test compressed file integrity:
```
pigz -t file.txt.gz
```

## Environment Variables

- **GZIP**: Options read from this variable before command line options
- **PIGZ**: Options read from this variable after GZIP but before command line options

## File Formats

pigz produces standard gzip, zlib, or zip format output. Any tool that can decompress these formats can decompress pigz output, and pigz can decompress any standard gzip file.

## Performance

The input is broken into chunks that are compressed in parallel. Each chunk is compressed independently with the last 32K of the previous chunk used as a dictionary to maintain compression effectiveness. The number of threads defaults to the number of available processors.

Decompression uses a single thread for the actual decompression, but creates additional threads for reading, writing, and checksum calculation.

## More Information

For complete documentation, see the pigz man page (pigz.1 or pigz.pdf).

## Author

pigz was written by Mark Adler.

.PP
Compressed files can be restored to their original form using
.I pigz -d
or
.I unpigz.

.SH OPTIONS
.TP
.B -# --fast --best
Regulate the speed of compression using the specified digit
.IR # ,
where
.B \-1
or
.B \-\-fast
indicates the fastest compression method (less compression)
and
.B \-9
or
.B \-\-best
indicates the slowest compression method (best compression).
.B -0
is no compression.
.B \-11
gives a few percent better compression at a severe cost in execution time,
using the zopfli algorithm by Jyrki Alakuijala.
The default is
.B \-6.
.TP
.B -A --alias xxx
Use xxx as the name for any --zip entry from stdin (the default name is "-").
.TP
.B -b --blocksize mmm
Set compression block size to mmmK (default 128KiB).
.TP
.B -c --stdout --to-stdout
Write all processed output to stdout (won't delete).
.TP
.B -C --comment ccc
Include the provided comment in the gzip header or zip central file header.
.TP
.B -d --decompress --uncompress
Decompress the compressed input.
.TP
.B -f --force
Force overwrite, compress .gz, links, and to terminal.
.TP
.B -h --help
Display a help screen and quit.
.TP
.B -H --huffman
Compress using the Huffman-only strategy.
.TP
.B -i --independent
Compress blocks independently for damage recovery.
.TP
.B -k --keep
Do not delete original file after processing.
.TP
.B -K --zip
Compress to PKWare zip (.zip) single entry format.
.TP
.B -l --list
List the contents of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -L --license
Display the
.I pigz
license and quit.
.TP
.B -m --no-time
Do not store or restore the modification time. -Nm will store or restore the
name, but not the modification time. Note that the order of the options is
important.
.TP
.B -M --time
Store or restore the modification time. -nM will store or restore the
modification time, but not the name. Note that the order of the options is
important. Modification times are stored only for regular files, not pipes.
.TP
.B -n --no-name
Do not store or restore the file name or the modification time. This is the
default when decompressing. When the file name is not restored from the header,
the name of the compressed file with the suffix stripped is the name of the
decompressed file. When the modification time is not restored from the header,
the modification time of the compressed file is used (not the current time).
.TP
.B -N --name
Store or restore both the file name and the modification time. This is the
default when compressing.
.TP
.B -p --processes n
Allow up to n processes (default is the number of online processors)
.TP
.B -q --quiet --silent
Print no messages, even on error.
.TP
.B -r --recursive
Process the contents of all subdirectories.
.TP
.B -R --rsyncable
Input-determined block locations for rsync.
.TP
.B -S --suffix .sss
Use suffix .sss instead of .gz (for compression).
.TP
.B -t --test
Test the integrity of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -U --rle
Compress using the run length encoding strategy.
.TP
.B -v --verbose
Provide more verbose output.
.TP
.B -V --version
Show the version of pigz. -vV also shows the zlib version.
.TP
.B -z --zlib
Compress to zlib (.zz) instead of gzip format.
.TP
.B --
All arguments after "--" are treated as file names (for names that start with "-")
.TP
These options are unique to the -11 compression level:
.TP
.B -F  --first
Do iterations first, before block split (default is last).
.TP
.B -I, --iterations n
Number of iterations for optimization (default 15).
.TP
.B -J, --maxsplits n
Maximum number of split blocks (default 15).
.TP
.B -O  --oneblock

# test quiet
echo "test quiet"

/workspace/executable -k -n t.txt
ls -l --time-style=full
/workspace/executable -l -v t.txt.gz
rm t.txt
/workspace/executable -d -n t.txt.gz
ls -l --time-style=full
cat t.txt

# reset
echo "time test" > t.txt
sleep 1
/workspace/executable -k -N t.txt
/workspace/executable -l -v t.txt.gz
rm t.txt
/workspace/executable -d -N t.txt.gz
ls -l --time-style=full

# -m option stores no time?
echo "time test" > t2.txt
/workspace/executable -k -m t2.txt
/workspace/executable -l -v t2.txt.gz
# -M stores time
/workspace/executable -k -M t2.txt 2>&1 || true
# test suffix with -c etc not delete
# test -c -k interaction
echo "keep c" > kc.txt
/workspace/executable -c -k kc.txt > out; ls -l kc.txt; rm out
/workspace/executable -c kc.txt > out; ls -l kc.txt; rm out
# test -f to compress .gz file
echo "gz file" > already.gz.txt
/workspace/executable -k already.gz.txt
ls
echo "try compress .gz again without -f"
/workspace/executable already.gz.txt.gz 2>&1; echo $?
ls
/workspace/executable -f already.gz.txt.gz 2>&1; echo $?
ls
rm already.gz.txt.gz.gz 2>/dev/null; true


# test -t verbose
echo "data" | /workspace/executable -c > good.gz
/workspace/executable -t -v good.gz 2>&1
echo "bad" >> good.gz
/workspace/executable -t -v good.gz 2>&1; echo $?

# test multiple files at once, stdin "-"
echo "hello" > one.txt
echo "world" > two.txt
/workspace/executable -k one.txt two.txt
ls -l
rm one.txt.gz two.txt.gz
cat one.txt | /workspace/executable -c - one.txt two.txt 2>&1 | head
ls -l
rm one.txt two.txt one.txt.gz two.txt.gz 2>/dev/null
echo "a" | /workspace/executable -c > one.txt.gz
echo "b" | /workspace/executable -c > two.txt.gz
/workspace/executable -d -c one.txt.gz two.txt.gz
# multiple decompress outputs?
# test -- handling
echo "dash file" > "-myfile"
ls
/workspace/executable -k -- "-myfile"
ls -l
rm -- "-myfile" "-myfile.gz"

# test zip comment
echo "zip comment" | /workspace/executable -K -C "zipcomment" -c > zipcomment.zip
/workspace/executable -l -v zipcomment.zip

# test copy of zopfli dir: contains COPY
cat /workspace/zopfli/CONTRIBUTORS
cat /workspace/zopfli/COPYING | head -20

# test rsyncable and independent implications
# Just ensure it produces valid output
echo "rsync" | /workspace/executable -R -c | /workspace/executable -d -c
echo "indep" | /workspace/executable -i -c | /workspace/executable -d -c

# Check behaviors when stdout is terminal?
# -f needed to output to terminal
echo "term" | /workspace/executable 2>&1 | head -c 20; echo exit:${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "term" | /workspace/executable -f -c 2>&1 | od -c | head

# list with stdin
echo "stdinlist" | /workspace/executable -c | /workspace/executable -l
cat good.gz | /workspace/executable -l

# Check what happens on decompress where output exists
echo "orig" > overwrite.txt
echo "new" | /workspace/executable -c > overwrite.txt.gz
/workspace/executable -d overwrite.txt.gz 2>&1; echo $?
cat overwrite.txt
echo "orig" > overwrite.txt
/workspace/executable -d -k overwrite.txt.gz 2>&1
echo "should not overwrite without -f"
cat overwrite.txt
/workspace/executable -d -f overwrite.txt.gz 2>&1; echo $?
cat overwrite.txt

# Clean and check decompress to stdout with file argument still keeps original?
echo "keepcheck" > keepcheck.txt
/workspace/executable -k keepcheck.txt
/workspace/executable -c -d keepcheck.txt.gz > out
ls keepcheck.txt* 

# Test with directory without -r
mkdir subdir
echo "file" > subdir/f.txt
/workspace/executable subdir 2>&1
/workspace/executable -r -k subdir && find subdir

# test -d -l -t mutual exclusion? 
# Try running with multiple incompatible? 
# Look for more edge case options

# print env GZIP handling order: GZIP then PIGZ then cmdline (cmdline overrides)
# Example: GZIP=-1 PIGZ=-9 should result in -9 ?
GZIP="-1" PIGZ="-9" /workspace/executable -v -c < a.txt 2>&1 | head -n 1
GZIP="-9" PIGZ="-1" /workspace/executable -v -c < a.txt 2>&1 | head -n 1
GZIP="-1 -v" PIGZ="" /workspace/executable -c < a.txt 2>&1 | head
echo "-9" | /workspace/executable -v 2>&1 # Actually -v alone shouldn't compress

# test -b parsing
/workspace/executable -b 32 -c < a.txt | wc -c
/workspace/executable --blocksize 32 -c < a.txt | wc -c
/workspace/executable -b 32K -c < a.txt 2>&1 | wc -c || echo "K not allowed?"

# test for -p n parsing
/workspace/executable -p 2 -c < a.txt | wc -c
/workspace/executable --processes 2 -c < a.txt | wc -c

# test for -S suffix dot?
/workspace/executable -k -S .tgz -c < a.txt > foo.tgz
ls foo.tgz
/workspace/executable -l foo.tgz

# test gzip suffix detection: .tgz ?
# gzip normally recognizes .tgz as gzip? but pigz?
echo "t" > bar.tgz
/workspace/executable -k bar.tgz -S .tgz 2>&1 || true
# Actually we need to compress with suffix .tgz
echo "content" > f
/workspace/executable -k -S .tgz f
ls f.tgz
/workspace/executable -d f.tgz
ls f

# behavior of unpigz: check argv[0]
cp /workspace/executable ./unpigz
./unpigz --help 2>&1 | head -n 1
echo "test unpigz" | ./unpigz -c | ./unpigz -c -d
rm ./unpigz

# More thorough check of -l output formatting
/workspace/executable -l -v comment.gz 2>&1
# check compressed output of empty file
cat /dev/null | /workspace/executable -c | /workspace/executable -l
cat /dev/null | /workspace/executable -c | wc -c
touch empty.txt
/workspace/executable -k empty.txt
/workspace/executable -l empty.txt.gz
/workspace/executable -l -v empty.txt.gz

# Check error messages for missing files?
/workspace/executable missingfile 2>&1
/workspace/executable -t missingfile.gz 2>&1
"}

{"command":"cd /tmp
rm -rf test2; mkdir test2; cd test2

/workspace/executable 2>&1
echo "---"
/workspace/executable -x 2>&1
/workspace/executable --unknown 2>&1
/workspace/executable -b 2>&1
/workspace/executable -p 2>&1
/workspace/executable -S 2>&1
/workspace/executable -C 2>&1
/workspace/executable -k -b notanumber -c < /dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
/workspace/executable -k -p notanumber -c < /dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
/workspace/executable -c -I notanumber < /dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
# Check help for unknown suffix handling?

# Test suffix detection for decompress
# For gzip, default suffixes?
echo "hi" > foo.gz
/workspace/executable foo.gz 2>&1; echo $?
cat foo.gz
rm foo.gz
echo "hi" > foo
/workspace/executable -k foo
ls
# pigz normally will not compress file that already has .gz suffix unless -f
# behavior for .zz and .zip ?
echo "hi" > bar.zz
/workspace/executable bar.zz 2>&1; echo $?
echo "hi" > bar.zip
/workspace/executable bar.zip 2>&1; echo $?
rm bar.zz bar.zip

# Test decompression suffix stripping
# Cases: .gz, .tgz, .zz, .zip?
# Let's see what gzip manual says: pigz should handle .gz, .tgz? Let's test:
touch a.gz
/workspace/executable -d a.gz 2>&1; ls; rm -f a a.gz
echo "x" | /workspace/executable -c > a.tgz
ls -l a.tgz
/workspace/executable -d -k a.tgz 2>&1; ls -l
# What about .zz?
echo "x" | /workspace/executable -z -c > a.zz
/workspace/executable -d -k a.zz 2>&1; ls
/workspace/executable -l a.zz 2>&1
rm a.zz
# .zip ?
echo "x" | /workspace/executable -K -c > a.zip
/workspace/executable -d -k a.zip 2>&1; ls
rm -f a a.zip

# Test decompress with suffix .foo (as earlier, custom suffix)
echo "content" > my.fa
/workspace/executable -k -S .fa.gz my.fa
ls my.fa.gz
/workspace/executable -d my.fa.gz 2>&1; ls
rm my.fa
echo "content" > my.fa.gz
/workspace/executable -d my.fa.gz 2>&1
# custom suffix .foo
echo "content" > s.myfoo
/workspace/executable -k -S .myfoo s.myfoo
ls s.myfoo.myfoo
/workspace/executable -d -S .myfoo s.myfoo.myfoo
ls s.myfoo

# Test with -S handling for decompress that file does not have compressed suffix
echo "content" > n.txt
/workspace/executable -k -S .mygz n.txt
ls n.txt.mygz
rm n.txt
echo "what happens if S mismatch?"
/workspace/executable -d n.txt.mygz 2>&1
/workspace/executable -d -S .mygz n.txt.mygz 2>&1; ls
rm n.txt.mygz n.txt 2>/dev/null; true

# Test --list with multiple files
echo "a" | /workspace/executable -c > l1.gz
echo "bb" | /workspace/executable -c > l2.gz
/workspace/executable -l l1.gz l2.gz
/workspace/executable -l -v l1.gz l2.gz

# Check list total line?
echo "a" | /workspace/executable -c > l1.gz
echo "bb" | /workspace/executable -c > l2.gz
echo "longer content here" | /workspace/executable -c > l3.gz
/workspace/executable -l l1.gz l2.gz l3.gz

# Test stdout combined? 
# Maybe -l with stdin?
cat l1.gz | /workspace/executable -l

# Check behavior of -t with verbose, test with multiple files?
/workspace/executable -t -v l1.gz l2.gz 2>&1; echo $?
# Corrupt one
cat l1.gz l2.gz > combined.gz
/workspace/executable -t combined.gz; echo $?

# Check behavior output file naming when decompressing with -c vs without
# Also check directory recursion with symlinks?

# Check compress to terminal without -f should fail
# Using script to detect isatty? We'll use bash to redirect?

# Check help for unpigz name detection: if binary called unpigz, defaults to -d?
# Our earlier cp failed due permissions, but let's try hardlink or symlink?
ln -s /workspace/executable /tmp/test2/unpigz
/tmp/test2/unpigz --help 2>&1 | head -n 5
# test that unpigz decompresses by default
echo "unpigz test" | /workspace/executable -c > up.gz
/tmp/test2/unpigz -c up.gz
echo "---"
# Does unpigz still compress if -c used? The name detection might force -d.
./unpigz -k up.gz 2>&1; ls -l up*
rm up up.gz 2>/dev/null
echo "unpigz default" | /workspace/executable -c > up.gz
./unpigz up.gz 2>&1; ls -l; cat up; echo "---"

# Test also gzip name? 
ln -s /workspace/executable /tmp/test2/gzip
/tmp/test2/gzip --help 2>&1 | head -n 1

# Clean
rm -f up up.gz a tgz etc
ls

"}

echo "hello" > n.txt

rm n.txt
/workspace/executable -d -z -S .abc n.txt.abc
ls n.txt
rm n.txt n.txt.abc

ls

ls n.txt

rm z z.zip
echo "zipcontent" | /workspace/executable -K -c > z.zip
/workspace/executable -d -K -k z.zip 2>&1; ls; cat z 2>&1
rm z z.zip

echo "zlibcontent" | /workspace/executable -z -c > z.zz
/workspace/executable -d -k z.zz; ls z; cat z
rm z z.zz
echo "zlibcontent" | /workspace/executable -z -c > z.zz
/workspace/executable -d -z -k z.zz; ls z; cat z
rm z z.zz

echo "second" > file.txt

echo "one" > one.txt
echo "two" > two.txt

/workspace/executable -d -c both.gz | od -c
rm both.gz one.txt two.txt

echo "data" > a.txt
/workspace/executable a.txt
ls a.txt 2>&1
echo "data" > a.txt
/workspace/executable -c a.txt > b.gz
ls a.txt

# Check symlink handling

/workspace/executable -k link.txt 2>&1; echo $?
/workspace/executable -k -f link.txt 2>&1; echo $?; ls link.txt.gz
rm link.txt link.txt.gz a.txt

# Check directory without recursive
mkdir d
/workspace/executable d 2>&1; echo $?
/workspace/executable -r d 2>&1; ls d

# Check -v output for compression
echo "some data to compress" > v.txt
/workspace/executable -k -v v.txt 2>&1
/workspace/executable -d -v v.txt.gz 2>&1
rm v.txt.gz v.txt
echo "some data" > v.txt
/workspace/executable -v v.txt 2>&1
ls v.txt.gz
/workspace/executable -d -v v.txt.gz 2>&1
ls v.txt
rm v.txt v.txt.gz 2>/dev/null

# Check -t -v output for good file
echo "ok" | /workspace/executable -c > ok.gz
/workspace/executable -t -v ok.gz 2>&1
/workspace/executable -t ok.gz 2>&1; echo $?

# Check -l -v with many options: comment appears on next line after file line?
echo "hi" | /workspace/executable -c -C "my comment here" > c.gz
/workspace/executable -l -v c.gz 2>&1
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess
out=subprocess.check_output(["/workspace/executable","-l","-v","c.gz"], text=True)
print(repr(out))
PY

echo "hi" | /workspace/executable -b 32 -c | wc -c

echo "hi" | /workspace/executable -A myname -c > out.gz

/workspace/executable -l -v out.zip
/workspace/executable -l out.zip

# Clean
cd /tmp; rm -rf suftest

import gzip
# inspect header
with open("f.txt.gz","rb") as f:

idx=10

    end=data.find(b'\x00', idx)
    print("fname:", data[idx:end])
    idx=end+1
if flags & 0x10:
    end=data.find(b'\x00', idx)
    print("comment:", data[idx:end])
    idx=end+1
if flags & 0x02:
    idx+=2

  /workspace/executable -d -S $suf -v a.txt$suf 2>&1; echo "decompress exit $?"
  rm -f a.txt$suf a.txt a.txt.tar
done

# Also test suffix without dot but with dash: -S mygz ? We saw mygz without dot compress creates a.txtmygz, decompress fails?

with open("out") as f:

    header=lines[0]
    data=lines[1]
    print(len(header))
    print(len(data))
    # Likely format: "%10d %10d %7s  %s" ? Let's examine
    # compressed field width maybe 10? Let's check
    # Example: "        10          8  -25.0%  a.txt"
    # compressed = 10 at positions 0-10
    # original = 8 at 11-21?
    # reduced = -25.0% ??? Let's count
    # Use regex
    import re
    # try to parse
    m=re.match(r'\s*(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+([-\d\.%inf]+)\s+(.*)', data)

    elif options['zip']:

        bio = io.BytesIO()
        entry_name = options['alias'] if options['alias'] else "-"

        # Create zip
        with zipfile.ZipFile(bio, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=comp_level) as zf:
            zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(entry_name)
            if options['store_time'] and is_file and input_name:

                    mtime2 = int(st.st_mtime)

            if level == 0:

        if comment:
            header += comment.encode('latin1', errors='ignore') + b'\x00'
        comp_obj = zlib.compressobj(comp_level, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)
        deflate_data = comp_obj.compress(data) + comp_obj.flush()
        crc = binascii.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff
        isize = len(data) & 0xffffffff
        trailer = struct.pack('<II', crc, isize)
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(header + deflate_data + trailer)
        return 0

ALLOWED_SUFFIXES = [".gz", "-gz", ".z", "-z", "_z", ".Z", ".tgz", ".zz", "-zz", ".zip"]

def prog_name():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) or "pigz"

def abort(msg):

    sys.exit(22)

def skip(msg, quiet):

        return
    sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_name()}: skipping: {msg}\n")

def warn(msg, quiet):

        return
    sys.stderr.write(f"{prog_name()}: warning: {msg}\n")

def parse_numeric_param(s, opt_char_for_err=None):
    # Try to parse int, with optional trailing K
    t = s
    # strip trailing K/k
    if t.lower().endswith('k'):
        t = t[:-1]
    try:
        if t == "" or t.lstrip('-').strip() == "":
            raise ValueError()
        # Check if integer
        # Allow leading +/-
        val = int(t)
        return val
    except:
        abort(f"invalid numeric parameter: {s}")

def format_timestamp(mtime):
    if mtime == 0:
        return "------ -----"
    try:
        dt = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(mtime)
    except:
        return "------ -----"
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    # If mtime is more than 6 months ago or in future, show year
    # Use days difference
    try:
        delta = now - dt
        if delta.days > 182 or delta.days < 0:
            # month abbrev, day width 2, two spaces, year
            return "%s %2d  %4d" % (dt.strftime("%b"), dt.day, dt.year)
        else:
            return "%s %2d %02d:%02d" % (dt.strftime("%b"), dt.day, dt.hour, dt.minute)
    except:
        return "------ -----"

def reduced_percent(comp, orig):
    if orig == 0:
        if comp == 0:
            return "  0.0%"
        return " -inf%"
    try:
        ratio = 100.0 * (1.0 - comp / orig)
        # Handle -0.0
        if abs(ratio) < 0.05:
            ratio = 0.0
        s = "%6.1f%%" % ratio
        return s
    except:
        return " -inf%"

def parse_gzip_header(data):
    if len(data) < 10:
        return None
    if data[0] != 0x1f or data[1] != 0x8b:
        return None
    flg = data[3]
    mtime = struct.unpack('<I', data[4:8])[0]
    idx = 10
    if flg & 0x04:
        if idx+2 > len(data):
            return None
        xlen = struct.unpack('<H', data[idx:idx+2])[0]
        idx += 2 + xlen
        if idx > len(data):
            return None
    fname = None
    comment = None
    if flg & 0x08:
        end = data.find(b'\x00', idx)
        if end == -1:
            return None
        fname = data[idx:end].decode('latin1', errors='ignore')
        idx = end+1
    if flg & 0x10:
        end = data.find(b'\x00', idx)
        if end == -1:
            return None
        comment = data[idx:end].decode('latin1', errors='ignore')
        idx = end+1
    if flg & 0x02:
        idx += 2
    return {'mtime': mtime, 'fname': fname, 'comment': comment, 'header_len': idx, 'flg': flg}

def get_output_suffix(opts):
    if opts['suffix'] is not None:
        return opts['suffix']
    if opts['zlib']:
        return ".zz"
    if opts['zip']:
        return ".zip"
    return ".gz"

def get_stripped_name(input_path, suffix_opt):
    # Determine output name for decompress
    # If suffix_opt is not None, must end with it and strip
    # Else find matching allowed suffix
    if suffix_opt is not None:
        if not input_path.endswith(suffix_opt):
            return None
        prefix = input_path[:-len(suffix_opt)] if suffix_opt != "" else input_path
        if suffix_opt == ".tgz":
            return prefix + ".tar"
        return prefix
    else:
        # find longest matching allowed suffix
        for suf in sorted(ALLOWED_SUFFIXES, key=len, reverse=True):
            if input_path.endswith(suf):
                prefix = input_path[:-len(suf)]
                if suf == ".tgz":
                    return prefix + ".tar"
                return prefix
        return None

def list_gzip_single(file_data, path_name, verbose, is_stdin=False):
    # file_data bytes, path_name for display (file name or <stdin>)
    # Returns comp, orig, check, mtime, fname, comment
    hdr = parse_gzip_header(file_data)
    if hdr is None:
        return None
    # Try to find member length via gzip
    bio = io.BytesIO(file_data)
    try:
        with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=bio, mode='rb') as gf:
            dec = gf.read()
            consumed = bio.tell()
            # deflate size
            deflate_size = consumed - hdr['header_len'] - 8
            # CRC and ISIZE from trailer
            trailer = file_data[consumed-8:consumed]
            if len(trailer) < 8:
                return None
            crc = struct.unpack('<I', trailer[0:4])[0]
            isize = struct.unpack('<I', trailer[4:8])[0]
            # For list, if multiple members, we need to sum? But we handle single for now
            # Check if there's more data after consumed (multiple members)
            # If remaining data starts with gzip magic, it's concatenated - we will handle separately in caller
            return {'comp': deflate_size, 'orig': isize, 'crc': crc, 'mtime': hdr['mtime'], 'fname': hdr['fname'], 'comment': hdr['comment'], 'consumed': consumed, 'dec': dec}
    except Exception as e:
        return None

                for relpath, content in files.items():
                    p = os.path.join(tmpdir, relpath)
                    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
                    if isinstance(content, bytes):

                    else:

            res={}
            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdir):
                for f in filenames:
                    fp = os.path.join(root, f)
                    rel = os.path.relpath(fp, tmpdir)
                    res[rel] = open(fp,'rb').read()

Zip list is hardcoded as pigz shows `0          0?  unk`.

Compression uses manual gzip headers (mtime, filename, comment) with raw deflate via `zlib`, zlib via `zlib.compress`, and zip via `zipfile`. Decompression detects gzip/zlib/zip magic, handles concatenated gzip members, trailing-junk warnings, and suffix checks replicating pigz's buggy custom-suffix logic (custom suffix must be in allowed list `.gz,-gz,.z,-z,_z,.Z,.tgz,.zz,-zz,.zip`). File handling includes symlink, directory, exists, empty, unrecognized format skips, recursive walk, `-c` stdout, `-k` keep, `-f` force, `-v` verbose messages, `-q` quiet suppression, and terminal detection for compress-to-tty abort.
